answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post offers or vote. A velvet interface may make signup feel effortless, but the thread linking an identity to its stake is on-chain: when independently audited behavior shows coordinated false claims, a challenge can slash the bond and distribute part to the challenger. Creating many sybils then multiplies the capital an attacker must immobilize and risk losing; jade-colored profile badges alone earn no extra trust. This raises attack cost without pretending stake proves a unique human.
